verdict: The r1 gap is genuinely and completely closed, and the fix is better than the one that was asked for. _condProbe() now normalises a map OR a (condition)=>number lookup, and I reproduced the critic's own case: with Wrecked drifted to 0.25, auditRigs(ids, (c)=>live[c]) now emits the identical 'condition "Wrecked" drifted: authority 0.25, mirror 0.3' string the map form emits, where r1 emitted nothing. Unfed inputs now push NOT CHECKED strings, and the flat-answer branch correctly distinguishes an unbound bridge lookup (all six keys answer 1) from real drift instead of firing five false alarms — that case is a genuine improvement over what the r1 critic asked for. All 15 acceptance criteria pass mechanically: node --check clean, exactly the ten pinned exports with the right arities, the six-row table matches the ratified numbers field-for-field, weights sum 100, effectiveRuns returns 2/1/3 on the worked cases, rollRig() returns null on an emptied table and the first entry on an all-zero weight column, ironback/GARAGE_*/discord/webhook all grep to 0, no imports, no window, and every trapped-global hit is inside a comment. Several hard-to-fake claims check out exactly: the 20-name PP_VEHICLE_NAMES mirror matches index.html:195562-195582 in order, the 'Rigs do not stack' quote is verbatim from 164427, the auction-slot defect it names is real at 196915 and honestly labelled unmeasured, and the price-band arithmetic (~195,800…~595,500 vs ~77,300…~235,000) reproduces to the hundred when you run it with the real mileage range. What stops it winning is a different defect from r1's: the file makes four confident factual assertions about index.html that are false, and one of them is load-bearing. In the block that justifies hardcoding economy numbers against a CLAUDE.md non-negotiable, it states 'there is nothing to route through TODAY: Transport has no OPS_ECON entry.' OPS_ECON.transport exists at index.html:79789 and _opEcon('transport') is already called at index.html:80431. That is a claim about another file's contents, presented as fact, used to excuse a rule the repo calls non-negotiable — in a file whose entire thesis is that two copies of a fact drifting apart is the enemy.
biggest_gap: The _opEcon justification block asserts a falsehood that was checkable at write time. rigs.data.js:92-96 says '_opEcon(t) (index.html:80021) ... returns null for a key it does not know, so there is nothing to route through TODAY: Transport has no OPS_ECON entry.' index.html:79789 is `transport: { startup: 650000, ratePerWorkerHr: 1000, salaryPerWorkerHr: 300, maxWorkers: 10, yields: {}, inputs: { fuel: 1.4 } }`, carrying an 18-line comment of its own, and index.html:80431 already calls `_opEcon('transport')`. The practical conclusion may survive (that entry holds no baseValue/runs field, so rig prices are still not on the dial) but the stated reason is wrong, and it is the reason a maintainer would trust instead of going to look. Fix inside the owned file: say what is actually true — OPS_ECON.transport exists and is the natural home, it currently carries startup/rate/salary/maxWorkers/yields/inputs and no rig-price fields, so baseValue/runs have no key to read yet — and keep the self-deleting instruction. While there, correct the same block's two other unverified numbers: the paid-rig fractions are 0.05/0.12/0.22 at index.html:164434, not '0.05, 0.12, 0.20', and _opEcon is at 80043, not 80021. Separately, ~18 exact index.html citations are stale by a uniform ~247-281 lines (PP_COND_MULT 195340->195587, PP_VEHICLE_NAMES 195315->195562, PP_CONDITIONS 195338->195585, PP_LOT_LEVELS 195401->195648, _ppGenListing 195910->196157, ppBuyVehicle 196009/196013->196289/196294, the auction slot 196634->196915, PPA_RARITIES 196457->196738, _ppaGenCar 196495->196776, the Garage header ~164198->164427, the photo grid 197455->~197737). builder_response: The critic was right and the file reproduced the exact inversion it warned about twelve lines earlier. Fixed inside the owned file, both parts. Part one: `_condProbe()` accepts a lookup FUNCTION as well as a map, and the drift block probes the six PP_CONDITIONS keys through it — verified by reproducing the critic's own case, where the function form now emits the identical `condition "Wrecked" drifted: authority 0.25, mirror 0.3` string the map form emits, having previously emitted nothing. Part two: an absent or unusable condMult now pushes a `NOT CHECKED` problem string, so an unfed alarm reads as "not checked" rather than "sound". Beyond the literal ask I handled the case the literal fix would have broken: the real caller's probe answers 1 for every key when the bridge is absent, which naively scored is five false drift lines against index.html; that is reported as an unbound lookup instead, while still naming a genuinely flattened PP_COND_MULT as the alternative cause so nothing is swallowed. The rarity ladder got the same treatment where it is cheap (an absent ladder is reported, since rule 1 derives its count from it), and the header now states why the vehicle-name list deliberately does NOT report itself — its mirror still checks against 20 real names, whereas condMult unfed checks nothing at all.
